name: playbook-runner
description: Run Ansible playbooks and manage vaults from a dashboard, discovered from the filesystem.

scripts.check: npm run lint && npm run typecheck && npm test
scripts.package: node -e "require('node:fs').mkdirSync('dist', { recursive: true })" && vsce package --no-dependencies --out dist/

untrustedWorkspaces.description: Playbooks and vaults are run as shell commands in the workspace folder, and the commands used come from settings that a workspace can carry.

virtualWorkspaces.description: Playbooks, inventories and vaults are read from disk and handed to ansible as filesystem paths.

playbookRunner.playbooksDir.description: Directory holding the playbook folders, relative to the workspace folder.

playbookRunner.rolesDir.description: Directory holding the roles, relative to the workspace folder — ansible.cfg's roles_path. Read when collecting the tags a playbook offers.

playbookRunner.inventoriesDir.description: Directory holding one subdirectory per environment, relative to the workspace folder.

playbookRunner.inventoryFile.description: Inventory filename. A directory under inventoriesDir counts as an environment when it contains this file.

playbookRunner.groupVarsDir.description: Group variables directory inside each environment.

playbookRunner.envFileName.description: Unencrypted variables filename inside each group_vars group. The dashboard links it on each service, opening it in the editor.

playbookRunner.vaultFileName.description: Vault filename inside each group_vars group.

playbookRunner.vaultPasswordFilePattern.markdownDescription:
Where to look for an environment's vault password file. Supports `${userHome}`, `${workspaceFolder}` and `${env}`. When the resolved file does not exist, `--ask-vault-password` is used instead. Set to an empty string to always be prompted.

User-level setting only: ansible executes a password file that is marked executable, so a workspace must not be able to point this somewhere else.

playbookRunner.vaultPasswordFiles.markdownDescription:
Per-environment vault password files, overriding `#playbookRunner.vaultPasswordFilePattern#`. Example: `{ "production": "${userHome}/.ansible-vault/prod.pass" }`.

User-level setting only, for the same reason as the pattern.

playbookRunner.productionPattern.description: Case-insensitive regular expression. Matching environment and task names are drawn in red and, unless confirmProduction is off, ask before running. Set to an empty string to disable.

playbookRunner.confirmProduction.description: Ask for confirmation before running a playbook against an environment matching productionPattern.

playbookRunner.ansiblePlaybookCommand.markdownDescription:
Executable used to run playbooks. Point this at a virtualenv if ansible is not on PATH; it is passed to the shell, so a wrapper such as `uv run ansible-playbook` works too.

User-level setting only: this is what gets executed, so a workspace must not be able to change it.

playbookRunner.ansibleVaultCommand.markdownDescription:
Executable used for vault create and edit.

User-level setting only, for the same reason as the playbook command.

playbookRunner.serviceEnvironments.markdownDescription: Environments that *Create Service Skeleton…* creates `group_vars/<name>/` in, by directory name under `#playbookRunner.inventoriesDir#`. Empty means every environment. A listed name that is not an environment (no `#playbookRunner.inventoryFile#`) is skipped and named in the confirmation — the command never creates an inventory.

playbookRunner.setupTags.markdownDescription: Tags whose tasks still run before the start of a task range (*From task* / *Only this task*), because the tasks after it need the facts they set. Empty makes *From task* behave exactly like `--start-at-task`.
